sources.entry: Seashore - Easy to use macOS image editing application for the rest of us.

summary.one_liner: Seashore is a free, easy-to-use layered image editing application for macOS.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Seashore as an image editing application for macOS that supports "layers." It is positioned as a simple, free alternative for users who want layered image editing without complexity. The README says it is available on the Mac App Store. It also notes that the project's original author was Mark Pazolli and that an older 0.6.6 release is distributed as binaries on the project's SourceForge site. The README gives no detailed feature list, build instructions, or screenshots text beyond a screenshots heading. It links to tutorial videos and a Libre Graphics World article, which is described as somewhat outdated.
use_cases: Editing images on a Mac with layers
Free alternative to paid macOS image editors
Running an older image editor on an old Mac
how_to_run: Install from the Mac App Store (README states it is on the App Store)
For macOS earlier than 10.9, download the 0.6.6 binaries from seashore.sourceforge.net (the 'hfs' version is suggested for older Macs)
notable: Layer-based image editing in a free, easy-to-use Mac app
Available on the Mac App Store
Legacy 0.6.6 binaries offered for older OS X versions
caveats: Current version requires macOS 10.9 or later
Development is being deprioritized in favor of Seahorse, per the README header
Older Macs need the legacy 0.6.6 binaries from SourceForge
